title: Get help for a shell builtin like cd
summary: Commands such as cd are built into the shell itself, so --help and the man command often show nothing useful for them. The shell's own help text describes them instead.

steps.explain: Check whether the command is built into the shell. Output 'is a shell builtin' means yes; output with a path such as /usr/bin/ls means it is a separate program, so use its --help or man page instead.

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: Name of the command you want help for

steps.expect: For cd: 'cd is a shell builtin'. For a separate program: a path such as /usr/bin/ls.

steps.explain: Show the built-in help text of the shell command. On macOS, the default shell zsh has no 'help' command; use the macOS variant to open the zsh builtins page, press / and type the command name to find it, then q to quit.

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: Name of the shell builtin, e.g. cd, echo or pwd

steps.expect: Text starting with the name and usage, e.g. 'cd: cd [-L|[-P [-e]] [-@]] [dir]' on Linux, then a description. Press q to leave the pager if one opens.

alternatives.explain: Bash only: print just the usage line of the builtin (on macOS bash 3.2 this is also the only short form).
alternatives.expect: cd: cd [-L|[-P [-e]] [-@]] [dir] on Linux; macOS bash shows 'cd: cd [-L|-P] [dir]'.

source.title: bash manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
